NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical intersection of advanced semiconductor manufacturing and AI infrastructure deployment, designing cutting-edge GPUs fabbed almost exclusively by TSMC on leading-edge nodes while supplying the dominant accelerated computing platform to hyperscalers, cloud providers, and enterprises worldwide. Its supply chain is characterized by extreme upstream concentration risk around TSMC and HBM memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung), while downstream demand is driven by a concentrated but rapidly expanding cohort of hyperscalers investing hundreds of billions in AI data center buildouts.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex, globally distributed supply chain, acting as a capital-light designer that outsources fabrication to foundries like TSMC while assembling through contract manufacturers (notably Foxconn/Hon Hai), giving it enormous purchasing leverage over hundreds of specialized component suppliers. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through carriers, its own retail and online stores, and a vast App Store/services ecosystem, making it both a hardware OEM and a platform gatekeeper that captures recurring revenue from developers, advertisers, and content partners worldwide.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, converting highly specialized capital equipment and raw materials from a concentrated group of suppliers into finished wafers for virtually every major fabless chip designer. Its irreplaceable position in advanced-node manufacturing (3nm, 5nm) creates an extraordinary chokepoint dependency, with top customers like Apple and NVIDIA relying almost entirely on TSMC for their most performance-critical silicon.

On the downstream side, IREN monetizes mined Bitcoin through cryptocurrency exchanges and OTC markets while simultaneously targeting hyperscalers and enterprise AI customers for its high-performance computing capacity, giving it a dual revenue model sensitive to both BTC price dynamics and AI compute demand.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at the intersection of nuclear fuel supply chains and next-generation clean energy delivery, depending critically on enriched uranium (particularly HALEU) suppliers and specialized nuclear component manufacturers to build its Aurora microreactors. On the downstream side, its primary customers are expected to be hyperscale data center operators and industrial energy consumers seeking reliable, carbon-free baseload power, though the company remains pre-revenue as of 2024 with all commercial relationships still in LOI or early-stage contracting phases.
